- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, check for over-optimism; true outcomes often overshoot early then correct, especially after high-event days.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model may underestimate downside risk; true prices often dip sharply after supply events.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model tends to overcorrect and forecast a slow decline — true outcome often rebounds or stabilizes, not fully reverses.
- When sentiment is mixed or negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, model may be ignoring bearish signals; true outcome often falls or stalls.
- Model tends to overestimate mean reversion in short-term (1-3d) after high volatility; true price often lingers or reverses after model’s “recovery” phase.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often underestimates volatility and over-predicts price stability — true outcome shows sharp swings, especially after auction supply events.
- If sentiment is bullish but model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, check for lag — true outcome often rises faster than model suggests, especially after bullish sentiment spikes.
- When supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model may overestimate price rise — true outcome often peaks then falls, especially after auction supply events.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment history when forecasting long-term (30d) — true outcome often reflects sentiment shifts more than model’s linear trend.
- If model forecasts are rising steadily with no recent negative sentiment, check for horizon bias — true outcome often shows a “reversal” or “pullback” after 10-15d, especially after high-event days.
